h: Yitzchak's Ushpiza: "His Seed Shall Be Mighty in the Land"

p: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (אֱמוֹר, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קד, א):
In the holy Zohar (Emor, Zohar III 104a):
'His seed shall be mighty in the land,' etc.,
'Wealth and riches are in his house,' etc."
"Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem" (ibid. 1),
which is the middah of 'Pachad Yitzchak';
for we find in the Gemara (Berachos 28b)
"like the fear of flesh and blood,"
that there is a greater fear than this,
that the King of kings stands over him;
and Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai said
is that the fear of Hashem always stands
as one standing before the King.
And the holiness of the Avos
so that it remained for their offspring;
just as a man begets a man
And the middah of Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
from which the positive mitzvos come;
for a lover does not hate;
for one who fears does not rebel."
and from love comes alacrity in the positive mitzvos,
to bring pleasure to his Beloved,
(as written in Rashi's commentary on the Rif,
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי אָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (חוּלִּין טז, א):
"Shall we arise and learn from Avraham?"
וְזֶה הִנְחִיל לְיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And this he bequeathed to Yitzchak Avinu, alav hashalom,
and this is what is said (Tehillim ibid. 1),
only his own middah, which he added,
And this is what is said,
"His seed shall be mighty in the land" (ibid. 2).
וְאִיתָא (סוֹף פֶּרֶק א דְּתַעֲנִית, טו, א):
And it is stated (end of the first perek of Taanis, 15a):
for one who overpowers his yetzer
needs the light of assistance from Hashem Yisbarach,
אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזֵר לוֹ
"Were it not that Hakadosh Baruch Hu helps him,
with the war against the yetzer
when one merits uprightness of heart,
emptying the evil out of the foolish heart —
And he left to his offspring:
"The generation of the upright shall be blessed";
"Wealth and riches are in his house" (ibid. 3).
"One who keeps company with harlots loses wealth" (Mishlei 29:3)
as referring to one who says, "This teaching is fine":
he loses the wealth of Torah.
And in its plain sense too one can say
that 'hon' means the wealth of Torah:
from which comes the fence against desires,
he loses the little wealth of Torah
"Why is there a price in the hand of a fool," etc.
those who occupy themselves with Torah
And likewise 'riches' refers to words of Torah,
"The rich and the poor" — of a rebbi and a student;
and likewise in Midrash Tanchuma (Ki Sisa 3):
"I am speaking of those rich in Torah," etc.
"Wealth and riches are in his house":
so that he does not lose wealth,
through the middah of Pachad Yitzchak.
And likewise 'wealth and riches' in the plain sense
through the middah of Pachad Yitzchak,
"And one who wishes to become rich should face north" —
"riches kept by their owner to his harm"
שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (מִשְׁלֵי ל, ח):
But through the middah of Yitzchak
and it will not harm him.
And so we find extraordinary wealth
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה תּוֹלְדוֹת סד, ז)
and not the silver and gold of Avimelech."
And this is what is said:
"Wealth and riches are in his house,
that it will not be spoiled.
"Light shines in the darkness for the upright"
for even the upright who merit simchah,
who seem not to need light,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם זוֹרֵחַ לָהֶם אוֹר גַּם כֵּן,
nevertheless light shines for them as well,
until all that they had attained
And the time on this day
is for meriting the holiness of Yitzchak,

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Nefesh David on the Zohar — “He merits to see children… as it brings the verse ‘His seed shall be mighty in the land’ (Tehillim 112:2); he merits in this world — this is ‘wealth and riches are in his house’; and he merits the World to Come — this is ‘and his righteousness stands forever.’ After it is written, ‘Light shines in darkness’ (Tehillim 112:4): darkness is turned to light, and all the masters of judgment cannot [harm him] — this is ‘gracious, merciful and righteous,’ that all is turned for him to mercy.” Connection: A commentary on the Zohar reading the same verses as three successive rewards, the three gifts Rav Tzadok finds in the mizmor.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 104a (Emor) — "Let a person not say, I will first eat and be satisfied and drink, and what remains I will give to the poor; rather, the first of all belongs to the guests. And if he gladdens the guests and satisfies them, the Holy One rejoices with him, and Avraham recites over him, 'Then you shall delight in Hashem' (Yeshayahu 58:14), and Yitzchak recites over him, 'No weapon formed against you shall succeed' (Yeshayahu 54:17). Rabbi Shimon said: That is what David the King said of him, for all the King's weapons and wars were entrusted into David's hands; but Yitzchak says, 'His seed shall be mighty in the land… wealth and riches are in his house' (Tehillim 112:2–3)."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 6 — “According to the Midrash Rabbah (Matos): three gifts were created in the world… one who merits wisdom merits everything, one who merits might merits everything, one who merits wealth merits everything — when they are gifts of Heaven and come through the power of Torah… Yitzchak merited might, as they said, ‘Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination.’” Connection: Both tie Yitzchak's might and wealth to gifts of Heaven that come through the power of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 28b — When R. Yochanan ben Zakkai fell ill, his students asked for a blessing. He said: "May it be [His] will that the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood." They said: "Only that much?" He said: "If only! Know that when a person sins, he says: Let no person see me." Rashi: would that you refrained from sin as you do before people. (Rav Tzadok attributes it to R. Eliezer.)

paragraphs.text: Chullin 16a — "From where do we know that slaughter is with something detached? As it says, 'And Avraham took the knife to slaughter' (Bereishis 22:10)… The verse comes to teach us the alacrity of Avraham."

paragraphs.text: Yoma 28b — "Rav Yosef said: Shall we arise and learn from Avraham? Rava said: The Tanna learned from Avraham, and we shall not learn from him? As it was taught: 'And on the eighth day he shall be circumcised' (Vayikra 12:3) — this teaches that the whole day is fit for milah, but the zealous hasten to mitzvos, as it says, 'And Avraham rose early in the morning' (Bereishis 22:3)."

paragraphs.text: Yoma 28b — "Avraham would pray [Minchah] as soon as the walls darkened… Shall we arise and learn from Avraham?" Rashi: to be zealous like Avraham.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 15a — "Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say: not all are for light and not all are for gladness. The righteous are for light, and the upright for gladness: the righteous for light, as it is written, 'Light is sown for the righteous' (Tehillim 97:11); and the upright for gladness, as it is written, 'and for the upright of heart, gladness.'"

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52b — "Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says, 'The wicked one watches the righteous and seeks to kill him' (Tehillim 37:32); and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, he could not overcome it, as it says, 'Hashem will not abandon him into his hand' (Tehillim 37:33)."

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 64a — "Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said: What is meant by 'But one who keeps company with harlots (ro'eh zonos) loses wealth' (Mishlei 29:3)? Whoever says, This teaching is fine (zo na'ah) and this one is not fine, loses the wealth of Torah." Rashi: its honor, and in the end it will be forgotten from him.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 72b — "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What is meant by 'Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when there is no heart (v'lev ayin)?' (Mishlei 17:16) — Woe to the enemies of Torah scholars [a euphemism for the scholars themselves] who toil in Torah but have no fear of Heaven." [Rashi does not comment on this line.]

paragraphs.text: Temurah 16a — "'The poor man and the man of means meet; Hashem lights up the eyes of both' (Mishlei 29:13): when the student goes to his teacher and says, Teach me Torah — if he teaches him, Hashem lights up the eyes of both; and if not, 'the rich and the poor meet; Hashem is the Maker of them all' (Mishlei 22:2) — He Who made this one wise makes him a fool, and the fool He makes wise."

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma, Ki Sisa 3 — "He said to them: I am speaking of those rich in Torah, not those rich in money. How so? A great man, rich in Torah, who taught many students and spread Torah in public — even after he dies, the students he raised do not let him sleep, but sit and occupy themselves with Torah… and say halachos and teachings in his name."

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 25b — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: One who wishes to become wise should face south, and one who wishes to become rich should face north; and your sign: the Table is in the north and the Menorah in the south." There also: "Out of the north comes gold" (Iyov 37:22).
